newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo fruitseller says he killed eight for cash.
newsitem.headline: Cairo fruitseller says he killed eight for cash.

text.p: An Egyptian fruit merchant said on Wednesday he had killed eight people including three women over the past seven years, most of them fellow traders he lured out of Cairo to remote farms on expeditions to buy fruit.

The man, Mostafa Abderrahim Othman, 43, would slip an insecticide into their food or drink to drug them, stab or strangle them to death and then steal all their money and valuables, said a detailed police report on his crimes.
"The devil tempted me. I was short of money, living in one room with eight children, my wife and my mother," Othman told a news conference organised by the Cairo police.
"I'm very sad for the victims. Every time I killed one I would feel very sorry and I would cry over the body," he added.

The police report said Othman killed first in 1989, when he took Abdelfattah Fahmi el-Sayyed on a trip to the northeastern province of Ismailia, poisoned him with the insecticide and stole 300 pounds (then about $130) from him.
"I was so relieved that I was not found out that I swore I wouldn't do it again," Othman told the news conference. "But in 1994 I needed money so I went back to killing."
He killed four people in the first six months of that year, including a young female cousin from the southern town of Sohag and a young male relative, for no apparent reason.
The police report said he took those two on an outing to Salhia, a thinly populated fruit-growing area northeast of Cairo, killed them and set fire to their bodies.
Othman also killed in anger, stabbing one man dead in the southern town of Minya during an argument and poisoning to death a Cairo drug dealer with whom he had quarreled.
His last victim, and the one whose death was traced to him, was Sayyeda Mohamed Mahmoud, a 47-year-old fruit merchant from the Cairo suburb of Rod el-Farag, where Othman also lived.

He took her to Abu Sweir in the northeastern province of Sharkia, also on a fruit-buying trip, drugged her, tried to rape her, and strangled with his hands and her scarf when she resisted, the police report said.
He smashed her face with a stick, knocking out three teeth, stripped her of her gold jewellery and stole 6,000 pounds ($1,760) which she was carrying, it added.
He then pressed her thumbprint onto one of her cheques, which he later tried to cash at her bank. Illiterates use thumbprints instead of signatures.
The police said they caught Othman because the woman was reported missing and someone had seen her in his company. Police searched his room and found stolen goods.
